subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits, burst behavior & overage pricing (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & pricing details from today's call - rate limits / burst / overage (Acme)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so engineering and procurement can evaluate pricing and quota options: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Expected baseline: ~25M tokens/month (in steady state)
- Burst profile: up to ~3x baseline (~75M tokens) for 1–2 hour windows, typically daily around batch job runs
- Target unit economics: aiming for $150–$200 per 1M tokens in overall blended cost (incl. support/observability)
- Budget range discussed: $4,000–$5,000/month initially (we gave a rough number on the call)

What I promised to follow up with: 
1) Pricing bands and examples (committed vs. on-demand) — attached sheet (ACME-Redwood-Pricing-Options.xlsx)
2) Rate limit behavior and burst policy (short summary below)
3) Overage terms & quota increase process
4) Next steps: agree on a short pilot (1mo) with a temporary burst quota increase, then evaluate committed capacity if traffic stabilizes

Rate limits / burst behavior (high level)
- Soft-burst allowance: Hosted customers get a configurable soft-burst allowance up to 3x committed throughput for short windows (default: up to 2 hours/day). During soft-burst we queue requests; latency may increase slightly but requests are not immediately rejected.
- Sustained usage above soft-burst: if you sustain >3x for >2 hours we'll throttle to the committed throughput and return 429s for excess requests.
- Per-route and per-key QPS limits apply; we can configure higher per-route quotas for API keys used by batch jobs.

Overage pricing & quota increases
- On-demand (no commit): standard price $220 per 1M tokens. Overage billed monthly.
- Short-term pilot discount: for trial pilots we can offer $160 per 1M tokens (applies to first 1M–50M tokens during pilot month).
- Committed (12mo) pricing: starts at $140 per 1M tokens for committed volumes >= 50M tokens/mo (tiered).
- Overage when committed: overage is charged at 1.5x the committed per-1M rate (e.g., committed $140 -> overage $210 per 1M).

Quota increase process
- Temporary increase: request via account team; typical turnaround 24–72 hours for hosted customers. We can provision a temporary soft increase window to cover scheduled bursts.
- Permanent committed increase: requires an amendment and billing commit (legal/finance review ~5–7 business days).

Next steps I propose:
- I will upload a tailored quote and the MSA draft (attached).
- Please confirm you want the 1-month pilot with a temporary burst increase and we will provision immediately once procurement signs the SOW.
- Camila and I will coordinate the quota request window if you provide preferred dates/times for the heavy jobs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15min sync if you want to review the numbers together.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side so procurement can size this: 
- Baseline: we can commit to 25M tokens/month to start.
- Bursts: the 3x number is accurate for our peak job; peaks last ~1–2 hours and happen nightly. Occasionally we have a one-off spike that was ~6x for <30 minutes during testing.
- Budget: the $4k–$5k number was a soft internal target; we are flexible if unit economics are better with a commit. Our procurement lead asked: do bursts count against committed volume or are they billed as overage? Also would temporary quota increases (for scheduled jobs) be subject to additional fees?

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the temporary burst window will be treated as part of committed TF or billed as overage if it exceeds the monthly commit?
2) Can you provide a sample monthly bill for the following scenario: 25M committed + one daily 2-hour 3x burst every day (estimate total tokens ~45M for the month) at the pricing tiers you listed?

If you can return that by tomorrow, I'll share it with procurement and we can move to sign-off.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Director of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
[Procurement: procurement@acme.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & pricing details from today's call - rate limits / burst / overage (Acme)

Alex —

Thanks — answers below and I've included a simple sample bill worked through the numbers (see inline).

1) Burst treatment vs. committed volume
- Bursts that are within the soft-burst allowance are not automatically treated as committed volume, they are allowed capacity above commit and billed as overage unless you convert the burst into a formal temporary commit.
- For pilots we typically treat scheduled temporary increases as a short-term amendment (no long-term commit) and bill overage at the pilot discount rate if arranged in advance.

2) Sample monthly bill (numbers illustrative)
- Committed volume: 25M tokens/month at committed pilot rate $160 per 1M = (25 * $160) = $4,000
- Burst usage: daily 2-hour 3x burst -> estimated monthly total tokens = 45M -> burst portion = 20M tokens over committed.
- If pilot discount applies to burst (agreed in advance): burst 20M at $160 per 1M = (20 * $160) = $3,200
- Total billed for month (pilot discount applied to all usage) = $7,200

If you do not opt into the pilot discount and remain on on-demand pricing: 
- Committed (none) would be billed at $220/1M; 45M tokens * $220/1M = $9,900

If you go committed 12mo at $140/1M (and burst overage at 1.5x committed $210/1M): 
- Committed 25M = 25 * $140 = $3,500
- Overage 20M = 20 * $210 = $4,200
- Total = $7,700

Temporary quota increases: we can provision a scheduled soft increase with 24–72 hour turnaround for hosted accounts; we can also arrange an explicit short-term amendment to treat scheduled bursts at the pilot rate (as above) to avoid high overage.

Next steps:
- If you want the pilot pricing (recommended to keep blended cost low), reply with preferred pilot window and we will produce a short SOW for procurement to sign.
- Camila, can you log the temporary quota request and flag for engineering so they can pre-provision the burst window once procurement signs?

Happy to run the numbers for any other combos you want.

Best,
Marissa
